assertion_analysis.failure_condition: assert report['refusal_count'] == 3 reddens if the dry run stops at its first refusal instead of gathering the sweep. Independently confirmed by the recorded negative control (negative-control.log: `_require_independently` mutated to keep only the first refusal, 1 failed with `assert 1 == 3`, EXIT=1), so the assertion is verified by reinstating the regression, not by observing green.

the emitted `invocation` is generated by `_dry_run_invocation` from the refusals' own text and is then executed by the test, and the test asserts exit_code 0 and that the pointer is gone. It fails if the invocation names a wrong flag, omits the gate status the check needs, or if the guards do not actually pass on the state the dry run described; the two sides (generator vs promotion) are independent.

the reason-flag test reddens if `_refuse_a_flag_as_a_reason` is dropped from the `--no-commit` option (crew_run_commands.py:1862): click would then accept `--gate` as the reason and exit 0. Independent of the value under test, since the assertion reads the parser's own refusal output.

`assert result['ledger_path']` reddens if the contracted receipt stops being read from the manifest (the command from `tests:`, the status from the log's `EXIT=0`), i.e. it guards the fill repair this node made; the fixture's inputs and the promotion's output are separate sources.

does not name a condition the code could fail: it holds for any dry run that leaves the pointer in place, including one that rewrites it. Not a guard for the write-nothing claim it is captioned with (see finding on this line).

findings.text: blocking: a dry run is not write-free on the withdrawn-run path. `complete()` reaches `return _complete_withdrawn_run(run_id, record)` (promotion.py:297) for any record whose project is empty, and that helper unlinks the live pointer and releases the workspace (promotion_records.py:187 `pointer_path(run_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)`) before returning a withdrawal dict, not a dry-run report. `crew complete --dry-run --run <id>` therefore destroys the pointer of exactly the run an operator would dry-run to inspect why it is stuck, contradicting the guard's own help text (crew_run_commands.py:2026, 'writing nothing: no ledger row, no plan comment, no pointer change') and the plan section's wording '--dry-run evaluates every guard without writing'. Reachable only through the flag this node adds, so it is the landed change that makes it reachable.

follow-on: two further side effects of `complete()` are inherited by the dry run because the `dry_run` branch sits after them. `_file_delivered_run_reviews(record)` (promotion.py:304) files a delivered review into the store, and `_await_in_flight_shadow_pick(run_id)` (promotion.py:283) can write a picker timeout onto the pointer; both are real writes on runs that carry a delivered review record or a deferred shadow pick, so 'writes nothing' is true of the golden path (project named, no in-flight pick, not a review run) rather than of the guard in general.

follow-on: `_command_from_gate_log` re-implements a capability the repository already owns. `reckon/crew/reports.py:1237 _test_log_command` already recovers the command a gate log names near its head, and it reads the same `# command:` label the capture convention writes (reports.py:1222-1230, matching `command:` or `cmd=` case-insensitively over the first 5 non-blank lines) and is the reader `_test_log_findings` uses to judge a manifest's cited logs. The addition reads first 10 raw lines and requires a literal `line.startswith('# command:')`, so it neither extends nor wraps the owner and the two can disagree about the same file: a log written `  # command: ...` (leading whitespace) or `cmd=...` is recovered by reports.py and missed here. The module already imports from reports.py at promotion_records.py:757, so calling `_test_log_command` was available without a new dependency.

blocking: the after-arm evidence the manifest cites no longer exists on disk. `after_suite.log_path` names gate-after.log, but that file was overwritten by the run's final re-run (stream.jsonl record 15293, 'Re-running the full gate at the final committed head so the after-arm log and its recorded revision agree') and the worker was terminated 22s later (exit.json ended_during=working, exit 143), leaving 3 lines, no pytest summary and no `EXIT=` line. `crew check-manifest --run r-20261019T105208473456-cso-complete-reports-every-refusal` run now returns ok:false with four findings: baseline_suite and after_suite 'not a flat suite record', the after_suite log naming cfb1d317 on its first line against the record's 0117d3e0, and 'test log ... ends with no EXIT=<n> line'. The done_when requires logs 'whose last line is EXIT=', so the after arm cannot be verified as recorded, and the record is inadmissible as it stands. Cause is the reuse of a log path across a retry; a fresh path per attempt leaves the cited evidence intact.

follow-on: the assertion guarding the no-write claim is weaker than the claim it accompanies. The comment says 'Nothing was written: the pointer survives for the run the dry run describes' but the assertion is `assert pointer_path(run_id).exists()`, which is satisfied by a pointer that was rewritten in place as readily as by one never touched -- the exact mutation the fill and the picker paths can perform. It would redden only on deletion, i.e. it guards none of the writes this review flags on promotion.py:283/297/304; asserting the pointer's bytes are unchanged is the check the comment promises.
